items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: Those guys had me playing my horn all night on the train, Herschel and a few of the others.

ctx.x: Yeah, I was going to ask you about that band. You were talking about the Tren. Right.
Well Herschel was playing alto in that band. And Jimmy Westbrook was playing the drums. He was not the left-handed drumming.
Who else was in the T&T? I can't recall. Big band, a small band?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: And sure enough he went ahead and blowed the roof off and got the job and we became real close friends and I'd help him.

ctx.x: Well what about Herschel Evans then? Was he a good reader when he came?

No, Herschel couldn't read music. How I met Herschel Evans, I was getting ready to leave here and they used to have the Dixie Series and there was a band that Herschel came here with, with a team from Wichita Falls that year. The name of this band was the TNT band and Jimmy Westbrook was the drummer, he's a left-handed drummer. He's now living in Los Angeles and Herschel was playing alto and playing a date up at the old Pelican ball and I met Herschel then and we all left on the same train. I was going to Dallas…

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: later on I had the opportunity of playing with one of the greatest tenor saxophone players that ever played. And incidentally I helped him along in his music career later on when I got in Troy Floyd's band.

ctx.x: Did you have a job when you left New Orleans or what were you doing?

Yes, we had a job off of us. We didn't know whether we were good enough for it or not because we only knew how to play three songs. What, do you remember what the three were? I Love You, The Sheik of Arabi were two of them. I can't remember the third one. But anyhow, after we got to Dallas, then there was a band traveling with me on the same train. It was the year that the New Orleans Pelicans were playing Wichita Falls in the Classic. And the fellas in this band, the T&T band, with some great musicians, later on…
I remember seeing a picture of Duke Ellington wearing pants like that.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-29
items.q: Even with some going back to 1926 when I first left here with Herschel Evans as an alto player.

ctx.x: We have Ollie Ross and Texas Tommy in your own band. Are there any ones you particularly want to hear or work on?

Well the time is so short Dick. I'm sorry it was like this. I most certainly want to spend some more time. Yeah well there'll be other trips. Yeah I understand. I would like to start next time from the beginning when I started and bring up some of the incidents that happened along with the big band that I had. Even with some going back to 1926 when I first left here with Herschel Evans as an alto player. Yeah.
I'd love to fill in all the details.
